Monica — quick sync of findings from infra side (summary):

Observed facts:
- Canary reserved GPU pool (pool-id: rsv-canary-7) is at 98% GPU utilization for sustained 30+ mins, queue depth increased 6x.
- Autoscaler did not provision additional nodes because a mis-tagged placement rule caused a portion of reserved traffic (approx 18% of BlueHarbor's requests) to be routed to the canary pool instead of their dedicated pool.
- The runtime also logged a transient kernel OOM on one node (seen in the attached error-samples), which increased retry loops inside the serving layer and amplified queueing.

Immediate mitigations (now):
1) Correct routing rule — we will apply the placement-tag fix to re-route the 18% misrouted traffic to BlueHarbor's dedicated pool (ETA 10m).
2) Emergency scale: add +2 GPU nodes to rsv-canary-7 to ease queue pressure (temporary, ETA 15m).
3) Apply a soft client-side guidance to BlueHarbor: reduce burst concurrency by 30% for 1 hour (we can provide parameter snippets).
4) Blacklist the affected node with kernel OOM and drain it for deeper inspection.

Probability of short-term recovery: high (70-80%) within 30–45 minutes after routing correction + scale.

If routing change is not possible due to config drift we will instead route a fraction of BlueHarbor traffic to a compatible fallback model cluster (latency slightly higher, but keeps throughput).

I'll implement 1+2 now and post back when done.

— Rishi
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

James / Marta — quick executive update and next steps after today's remediation: 

What happened (TL;DR):
- Root cause: configuration drift caused ~18% of BlueHarbor reserved traffic to be routed to our canary reserved pool (rsv-canary-7). That pool subsequently hit saturation and a node experienced a transient kernel OOM causing retries and amplified queueing.

What we did: 
- Corrected placement tags to re-route traffic to BlueHarbor's dedicated pool (completed 2027-06-20T09:58 PT).
- Emergency +2 GPU nodes added to rsv-canary-7 and the affected node drained for inspection.
- Provided BlueHarbor guidance to temporarily reduce burst concurrency while we validated the fix.

Current status: throughput returned to within SLA thresholds by 10:30 PT on 2027-06-20; error rates normalized and queue depth has been stable. We retained logs and samples (attached).

Action items and risk mitigation (next 7 days):
- Ops: run placement-tag audit across reserved deployments (owner: infra-config team) — ETA 72 hours.
- Eng: investigate kernel OOM root cause on that node (owner: runtime team) — ETA 5 business days.
- AM/Customer: Monica/BlueHarbor to confirm any customer-side spike patterns that could have triggered memory pressure.
- Finance/Sales: Lauren/Stephanie to advise on credit posture; engineering estimates incident <2 hours of customer-visible impact, propose goodwill credit instead of full SLA penalty as initial remedy.

Related artifacts: pool-usage-20270620.csv, error-samples-06-20.txt attached; HubSpot DH-4821 updated with incident notes: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/DH-4821.

We apologize for the disruption — we're treating this as high priority to prevent recurrence. Lauren / Stephanie, happy to discuss conservative credit language and a short customer note.
